 CDC: E. coli Outbreak Tied to Frozen Blueberries Ends, But Recall Expands 
 Dani Tietz 3 weeks ago 0 1 minute read

 Pocket 
 A multistate outbreak of E. coli infections linked to frozen organic blueberries has ended after sickening 17 people and hospitalizing six, federal health officials said. No deaths were reported.
 The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention closed its outbreak investigation Sept. 21, but consumers are still being urged to check their freezers because additional frozen berry products were added to the recall in early October. The recalled products carry “best by” dates extending into 2028. Health investigators identified frozen organic blueberries supplied by Frutas y Hortalizas del Sur S.A. of San Carlos, Chile, as the source of the outbreak.
 On Oct. 2, the supplier expanded its recall to include additional lots of Great Value frozen organic products and a Trader Joe’s mixed berry product. The FDA says consumers should not eat, sell or serve recalled products.
 The expanded recall includes:
 Great Value Organic Triple Berry Blend, 10-ounce packages, with lot codes 6 031 01 and 6 041 01 and “Best If Used By” dates of Jan. 31, 2028, and Feb. 10, 2028.
 Great Value Organic Blueberries, 10-ounce packages, with lot codes 6 019 01, 6 040 01 and 6 163 01 and dates ranging from Jan. 19, 2028, through June 12, 2028.
 Trader Joe’s Organic Mixed Berry Blend, 12-ounce packages, lot code 6 051 01, with a “Best Before” date of Feb. 20, 2028.
 Earlier recalls included all lots of Publix GreenWise Organic Whole Blueberries and Whole Mixed Berries, as well as a recalled lot of Great Value Organic Triple Berry Blend sold at Walmart.
 Consumers should check their freezers for recalled berries, including products that may appear old because of their long shelf dates. Recalled products should be thrown away or returned to the retailer for a refund, according to the CDC and FDA.
